title: Male lifestyle and fitness influencers in Australia | MANA
description: What male lifestyle and fitness influencers in Australia reach, why the audience is often offshore, what brands book them for and how to check the numbers.
h1: Male lifestyle and fitness influencers in Australia: reach, audience and how brands book them
lede: Male lifestyle and fitness influencers in Australia reach young men aged 18 to 34 with day-in-the-life, training, self-growth and student-life content, and much of that audience sits outside Australia. The ones worth booking are judged on views and non-follower reach over 90 days, on shares, and on whether the brand can be shown inside the creator's own format.

sections.h2: What does a male lifestyle creator's audience look like?
body: The lists online rank these accounts by followers and by how fit the creator looks. Neither predicts what a sponsored reel will do. Lifestyle and self-growth content travels almost entirely on Instagram's recommendation feed, so the numbers that matter are 90-day views, average views per reel, the share of viewers who do not follow the account, shares and reposts, and the audience's age, gender and location.

One example from the MANA roster, [Preston Young](/creators/preston-young), is a Melbourne creator and University of Melbourne student who makes cinematic, story-led reels on life lessons, self-growth, day-in-the-life, student life and fitness. Over a 90-day window from June to September 2026 his Instagram insights showed 1.86M views, 81K average views per reel, 86.6% of reach from non-followers and 1.09M unique viewers. Six reels passed 750K views in twelve months; the largest reached 2.9M views with 58.2K shares and 30K reposts. The audience is 65% men, two in three aged 18 to 34, with the United States, the Philippines and Indonesia as the top three markets and Singapore the biggest single city.

That last point is the one brands miss. An Australian male lifestyle creator often reaches more young men in the US and Southeast Asia than in Australia. For a brand that ships to those markets it is the whole value; for a brand that only ships in Australia it is the first question to ask.
bullets: 90-day views and average views per reel, from Instagram insights, dates shown
Share of reach from non-followers (above 80% is common for story-led reels)
Shares and reposts, which carry self-growth content further than likes do
Gender split and age bands, so a men's product is actually reaching men aged 18 to 34
Top countries and cities, checked against where you ship

body: Few Australian male creators are fitness-only accounts with a brand audience; most of the reach sits with lifestyle creators for whom training is one pillar among several. That is good for most brands. A supplement, a piece of training kit, a recovery product or an app lands better inside a day-in-the-life or a lesson-format reel than inside a workout clip that looks like every other workout clip.

On the MANA roster, Preston's pillars are life lessons, self-growth, day in the life, student life, fitness and Asian culture. [Kevin Chiang](/creators/kevin-chiang), also in Melbourne, reaches a different slice of the same age group through architecture, design and student-life content, with health and running among his audience's interests, 928K+ monthly views and an even gender split. Between them a men's brand can reach the self-growth audience and the design-minded student audience from one media kit.

sections.h2: What do brands book male lifestyle and fitness creators for?
body: Supplements and nutrition, training and recovery products, audio and tech that fits a routine, apparel, grooming, finance and productivity apps aimed at young men, and education products. The format that works is the creator's own: a lesson, a routine, a day, with the product doing something inside it. Brands get three kinds of deliverable: an organic reel or carousel on the creator's account, a partnership ad run from the creator's handle, or UGC made for the brand's own channels and ads with usage rights agreed up front.

Two rules from the deals that worked. The brand supplies the facts and the must-say and must-not-say lines in writing, and the creator writes the script. And usage is decided before filming, not after the reel does well. [How to brief a creator](/journal/how-to-brief-a-creator) and [usage rights and whitelisting, explained](/journal/usage-rights-and-whitelisting-explained-for-brands) cover both.

sections.h2: How much do male lifestyle influencers in Australia charge?
body: Per deliverable, not per follower. An organic reel, a carousel, a story set, a reel with a partnership ad, raw UGC footage or an edited UGC reel are each priced on their own, and three things move the price: usage period and placements, whitelisting, and category exclusivity. Health and finance briefs often carry a premium because of the claims checking involved.
MANA does not publish rates. Ask for the media kit and a quote for your exact scope, and compare the quote against the audience data rather than against follower counts.

Send the product, the market you want to reach and the live date, and ask for the media kit. You get current insights, the formats that fit and a quote. Deliverables, revisions, usage, whitelisting, exclusivity and dates go in writing before anything is filmed. [MANA](/brands) usually replies within a day.

faq: Who are the male lifestyle influencers in Australia brands can book?

Mostly lifestyle and self-growth creators for whom fitness is one pillar, reaching men aged 18 to 34 and often reaching the US and Southeast Asia as much as Australia. Preston Young in Melbourne is one example: 1.86M views in 90 days, 86.6% non-follower reach, 65% male audience.
Do Australian male fitness influencers reach an Australian audience?

Not always. Story-led reels travel on the recommendation feed, so an Australian creator's top markets can be the United States, the Philippines and Indonesia. Check top countries and cities in the insights before you book, and match them to where you ship.
What do male lifestyle and fitness influencers charge in Australia?
Per deliverable, with usage, whitelisting and exclusivity moving the price, and a premium on health and finance briefs. MANA quotes for your exact scope and does not publish rates.
